mutations.name: F1 the catch in publishPresence records unconditionally, so a put that outlives its epoch writes presence-refusal state belonging to a later connection: held across stop() it re-plants the record on the stopped endpoint, and held across a rebuild it plants one on the connection that replaced it (heartbeat 2s against a ~5s put timeout, so a rebuild finishing inside that window is the common case, not a corner). This suite imports @cotal-ai/core, which resolves to dist/, so the command builds core first and afterRestore rebuilds it: without that rebuild the tree keeps a dist/ compiled FROM THE MUTANT after the source is restored, and dist/ is gitignored so git cannot be the recovery.
mutations.replace:
this.presenceWriteFailingSince ??= Date.now();
      this.lastPresenceWriteError = (e as Error)?.message ?? String(e);
mutations.expectRed: a presence put that settles AFTER stop() does not resurrect the record on the stopped endpoint
